title: The kernel of a surjection of flat modules is flat
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $0\to M'\xrightarrow{u}M\xrightarrow{v}M''\to0$ a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] of $R$-modules. If $M$ and $M''$ are flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $M'$ is flat.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00HM (lemma-flat-ses), second assertion, line 9071

proof.text: Criterion. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fg-ideal-criterion] (Stacks 00HD, (4) implies (1)) it suffices to show: for every finitely generated ideal $I\subset R$ the multiplication map $\mu_{M'}:I\otimes_RM'\to M'$, $x\otimes m'\mapsto xm'$, is injective. Fix such an $I$ and write $\mu_M:I\otimes_RM\to M$ likewise.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00HM (lemma-flat-ses), proof, lines 9078-9094: 'We will use the criterion that a module N is flat if for every ideal I the map N (x) I -> N is injective, see Lemma 00HD'

proof.text: The diagram. The square with top row $u:M'\to M$, bottom row $\mathrm{id}_I\otimes u:I\otimes_RM'\to I\otimes_RM$ and vertical maps $\mu_{M'}$, $\mu_M$ commutes: on generators $\mu_M((\mathrm{id}_I\otimes u)(x\otimes m'))=\mu_M(x\otimes u(m'))=x\,u(m')=u(xm')=u(\mu_{M'}(x\otimes m'))$ by $R$-linearity of $u$, and both composites are additive, so they agree on all of $I\otimes_RM'$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00HM (lemma-flat-ses), proof, lines 9078-9094: the diagram with rows 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0 and M' (x) I -> M (x) I -> M'' (x) I -> 0

proof.text: Two injective arrows. (a) Since $M$ is flat, $\mu_M$ is injective, by the direction (1) implies (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fg-ideal-criterion]. (b) Since $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ is exact and $M''$ is flat, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] (Stacks 00HL), applied with $N=I$, shows that the lower left arrow $\mathrm{id}_I\otimes u:I\otimes_RM'\to I\otimes_RM$ is injective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00HM (lemma-flat-ses), proof, lines 9078-9094: 'if M'' is flat then the lower left horizontal arrow is injective by Lemma 00HL'

proof.text: Diagram chase. Let $z\in I\otimes_RM'$ with $\mu_{M'}(z)=0$. By the commutative square (step 2), $\mu_M((\mathrm{id}_I\otimes u)(z))=u(\mu_{M'}(z))=0$; $\mu_M$ is injective (step 3a), so $(\mathrm{id}_I\otimes u)(z)=0$; $\mathrm{id}_I\otimes u$ is injective (step 3b), so $z=0$. Hence $\mu_{M'}$ is injective for every finitely generated ideal $I$, and $M'$ is flat by step 1. (Stacks writes the composite chase as 'the second follows'; the injectivity of $u$ itself is not needed.)
